title: Poland's Inflation Uptick Tests Government Claims That the Cost-of-Living… · 15 Aug
keywords: Poland, inflation, cost of living, fuel prices, VAT reduction, Donald Tusk, NBP, monetary policy, EU economy, household budgets, price intervention, Polish economy, CPI, fiscal policy, European Union
notes: Polish inflation accelerated to 3.0 percent in July, up from 2.5 percent in June, complicating the government's narrative that price pressures are firmly under control. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has responded by announcing a temporary fuel-price intervention for the final two weeks of August, including a reduced VAT rate and daily price caps. The measures offer short-term relief but have drawn accusations of political timing ahead of the autumn season. The episode illustrates a tension playing out across the European Union: how to balance household affordability, fiscal credibility, and electoral politics.
